topic: BUG: Admin user cannot open tabbed pages in React — JWT roles double-serialized as JSON string
query: Admin users cannot navigate to any tabbed page in the React frontend. Root cause: JwtService.generateToken() serializes roles as a JSON string via objectMapper.writeValueAsString(), then stores it as a JWT claim string. When usePermissions.js decodes the JWT, claims.roles is a JSON string like '[{"role":"SUPER_ADMIN"}]' — the hook parses it correctly. However, the roles are stored as List<Map<String,Object>> (objects with a 'role' key), and the hook maps them via r.role. This should work for SUPER_ADMIN. The real issue is likely that the admin user's JWT has empty roles (task #14 — JWT roles empty). If the roles array is empty, usePermissions falls through all checks and returns all-false permissions, making every page appear blank/inaccessible. Secondary issue: AuthContext.fetchPermissions() calls /api/auth/permissions which may return 403 for admin, causing allowedApiList to be empty — though this is legacy code and usePermissions reads JWT directly. Need to verify: (1) what roles the admin JWT actually contains, (2) whether the /api/auth/permissions endpoint works for admin.
completionNotes: Same root cause as #14 — disabled tabs were caused by REAW template mismatch (tabOrder 1-based vs 0-based check), not JWT permissions. Fixed.

topic: Analysis: Admin cannot open tabbed pages — full code trace
query: Traced the full flow: LoginPage -> AuthContext.setAuth -> ProtectedRoute (auth-only, no role check) -> AppLayout (renders all nav unconditionally) -> Page component -> DataTable -> usePermissions(basePath). The usePermissions hook decodes JWT, extracts roles, and checks for SUPER_ADMIN. JwtService stores roles as JSON-serialized string of List<Map<String,Object>> e.g. '[{role:SUPER_ADMIN}]'. The hook handles this: parses the string, maps r.role. If SUPER_ADMIN is present, full access is granted. So the hook logic is correct IF the JWT actually contains the role. This bug is likely connected to task #14 (JWT roles empty after setup). If the admin user has no roles in the JWT, usePermissions returns all-false, and while the page renders, the DataTable shows no action buttons and the data fetch may fail with 403 from the backend.
response: Two possible root causes: (1) Admin JWT has empty roles — connected to task #14. (2) The /api/auth/permissions endpoint (called by AuthContext on login) fails for admin, though this is legacy and usePermissions reads JWT directly. Need to decode an actual admin JWT to confirm.

topic: Fix plan for task #44: Admin tabbed pages bug — full code trace and hypotheses
query: Traced the full auth chain: SetupService.createSuperUser() inserts SUPER_ADMIN role -> AuthService.buildJwtClaims() queries user_role table and builds roles as List<Map> -> JwtService.generateToken() serializes to JSON string in JWT -> JwtAuthenticationFilter extracts roles from JWT, sets on AuthUser transient field, puts into security context -> usePermissions.js decodes JWT, parses roles, checks SUPER_ADMIN. Logic chain looks correct on paper. Two hypotheses: (A) user_role table has no rows for admin — SetupService uses @Transactional with reactive chain, role save may fail silently, JWT gets empty roles, usePermissions returns all-false. (B) validateToken succeeds but roles extraction fails silently. Fix plan: 1) Query user_role table to confirm data. 2) If no role row: fix swfaw SetupService template with explicit error handling, add USER role alongside SUPER_ADMIN, add startup check. 3) If role exists but JWT empty: add logging to buildJwtClaims, check extractRoles deserialization. 4) React hardening: usePermissions should warn on empty roles, show error instead of blank page.

topic: DELETE bug deeper root cause: AuthorizationWebFilter causes double handler invocation
query: Debug logging confirmed the delete service method runs TWICE per request. First run succeeds (finds entity, logs delete, deletes, cleans up record_owner). Second run fails (entity already deleted, throws EntityNotFoundException -> 404). Root cause: AuthorizationWebFilter uses handlerMapping.getHandler(exchange) which in Spring WebFlux resolves AND triggers handler execution. Then DispatcherHandler invokes the handler again. This is NOT a service template issue — it's an AuthorizationWebFilter issue. The @ResponseStatus(NO_CONTENT) and .then() fixes are still correct but insufficient because the 404 comes from the second invocation. Fix options: (1) Cache the handler resolution result in the exchange attributes so it's not re-invoked, (2) Use a different approach in AuthorizationWebFilter to read annotations without triggering handler execution, (3) Change the filter to use exchange attributes to mark 'already authorized' and skip on second pass.
response: Previous fixes (no-args getCurrentUser, .then(), @ResponseStatus) are all correct improvements but don't address the double invocation. The AuthorizationWebFilter template needs fixing.

topic: FIXED: DELETE 404 bug — replaced AuthorizationWebFilter with AuthorizationAspect (AOP)
query: Root cause was AuthorizationWebFilter calling handlerMapping.getHandler(exchange) which caused double handler invocation. Fix: moved authorization from WebFilter to AOP aspect (AuthorizationAspect). Authentication stays in JwtAuthenticationFilter WebFilter. AuthorizationAspect uses @Around advice on @TableAccess and @QueryAccess annotations — runs once per controller method invocation, no double invocation. Changes: (1) New AuthorizationAspect template in authorization_service_templates.py, (2) Removed AuthorizationWebFilter from SecurityConfig template, (3) Added spring-boot-starter-aop to pom template, (4) Added generator method in authorization_service_generator.py, (5) Added generation call in main.py. All CRUD operations verified: CREATE 200, GET 200, UPDATE 200, DELETE 204, GET-after-delete 404.
